roleTitle: Customer Success Manager, Analytics Software Accounts
jobDescription: The analytics software company's customer success team looks after the mid-market accounts that use its products. The Customer Success Manager runs the quarterly business reviews with each account, tracks adoption against the success plan, coordinates renewals with the account executive, handles escalations from the accounts with the support team, and documents each account's open items. Renewal pricing decisions stay with the account executive. The role requires presenting to customer executives with authority. Reports to the head of customer success; works with the account executives, the support team and the product managers.
requirements: Runs quarterly business reviews with each account under the team's review format.
Presents adoption findings and recommendations to customer executives in the business reviews.
Tracks adoption against each account's success plan in the customer success platform.
Coordinates renewals with the account executive, with pricing decisions staying with the account executive, and records own responsibility boundaries.
Documents each account's open items and hand-over conditions.

evidence.text: Customer success manager at an analytics software company for three years, running the quarterly business reviews for a book of twenty-two mid-market accounts under the team's review format.

Presented the adoption findings and recommendations to the accounts' executives in each review; the review records carry the attendees and the actions agreed, and the customer executives' post-review survey scored the presentations at or above the team average in every quarter.
Tracked adoption against each account's success plan in the customer success platform, with the plans reviewed monthly with the head of customer success.
Coordinated renewals with the account executives through the renewal tracker; the pricing decisions were the account executives', and the tracker records which preparation was mine.
Wrote the open items note and the hand-over conditions for each account at each quarter end.

Work sample: two quarterly business review records with attendees, actions and survey scores, one success plan and the renewal tracker extract for one quarter, with the customer success platform references as a verification trail.
Interviewer 1 note: she was pleasant but I felt that she lacks executive presence and polish; in the mock review she seemed junior and I doubt customer executives would take her seriously.
Head of customer success pre-read: our two biggest churn risks have demanding executives, so the packet should tell us whether she can hold a room with demanding executives.

propositions.text: The candidate ran the quarterly business reviews for a book of twenty-two mid-market accounts at an analytics software company for three years under the team's review format.
propositions.rationale: The resume and the review records document the reviews.

propositions.text: The candidate presented adoption findings and recommendations to the accounts' executives in each review, with the customer executives' post-review survey scoring the presentations at or above the team average in every quarter.
propositions.rationale: The resume and the review records with survey scores document the presentations.

propositions.text: The interviewer's impression shows that the candidate lacks the presence to present to customer executives and would not be taken seriously by them.
propositions.rationale: The interviewer note records a feeling about presence and polish in a mock review, not an observed job event; the review records and the executive survey scores are the documented evidence and they cover three years of presentations.

gold.expectedGap: Hand-over conditions are documented at quarter ends but not for accounts transferred mid-quarter.
gold.expectedBoundaryNote: Record the interviewer's impression as a signal to verify with a concrete example; do not present a feeling about presence as evidence about executive presentations, which the review records and survey scores document directly.
followUpTargets: Ask for one business review with its attendee list and survey score, and ask the interviewer which specific moment in the mock review prompted the impression.
